chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibrahim ibn Abi Sammaq from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When you enter Mecca while you are in the state of Tamattu' (combining Hajj and 'Umrah), and you see the houses of Mecca, cut off the Talbiyah. The boundary of the houses of Mecca that existed before today is when you reach the Pass of the Madinan people; there cut off the Talbiyah. And you should continue with Takbir, Tahliq, and praising your Lord Allah as much as you can. And if you are Qarin (combining Hajj and 'Umrah together), do not cut off the Talbiyah until the Day of 'Arafah at the time of the sun's decline. And if you are Mu'tamir (performing 'Umrah), cut off the Talbiyah when you enter the Haram."

key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةَ: The ritual declaration of 'Labbayk' recited during Ihram
key_terms.عَقَبَةَ الْمَدَنِيِّينَ: A specific pass or boundary in Mecca
key_terms.قَارِنًا: A pilgrim who combines Hajj and 'Umrah together without breaking Ihram
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٌ: A pilgrim who performs 'Umrah first, then Hajj, with a break in between

ai.seo_question: When should a pilgrim stop reciting Talbiyah during Hajm based on their type of Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the precise moments for terminating the Talbiyah based on the type of Hajj, reflecting the scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between the ritual states of Tamattu', Qarin, and 'Umrah. It highlights the transition from the general declaration of God's greatness to the specific focus of the pilgrimage, with boundaries marked by the entry into Mecca's residential areas or the time of solar noon on the Day of Arafat. This ruling underscores the structured nature of Hajj rituals in Shia jurisprudence, linking physical movement with spiritual milestones.
